subpage_title: The Fredrik Roos Scholarship exhibition 2026: Kim Andreas Roland Berger – Accumulated Stacks
event_description: The artist Kim Andreas Roland Berger has been awarded the Fredrik Roos Art Grant for 2026. In connection with the award, Artipelag presents Roland Berger’s grant exhibition, Accumulated Stacks. Kim Andreas Roland Berger (b. 1993 in Oslo) uses drawing, painting and sculpture in his material-based and process-oriented practice.

At the turn of the 20th century, Alphonse Mucha was one of the most famous artists in Europe. A key figure of Art Nouveau and the inventor of an original style of graphic art, his work combined female beauty and stylised nature with a resolutely innovative composition and typography. The “Mucha style” has been a source of fascination ever since it was created and was applied to a variety of artworks and objects that adorned art lovers’ homes around the world at the time. Welcome to an immersive experience for all ages!

Quarnevalen is one of Sweden’s most spectacular student events, a proud tradition of joy and creativity since 1910. Students from across Stockholm design and build their own creations and parade them before an audience of half a million spectators. It’s the birthplace of innovation and future leaders, even the King once took part as a builder! Quarnevalen is more than a celebration; it’s an essential part of Stockholm’s cultural life.

In this all-Italian program with Ensemble BaraBarock, tears, jealousy, desire, and ecstasy resonate. In the Venice of love, there is "the Red Priest" Antonio Vivaldi, one of the most significant composers of the Baroque era.

The hit musical & Julia, which revolves around Max Martin's unique music catalog, is finally being staged at home in Sweden. For several years, the audience- and critically acclaimed musical has filled the halls of the West End and Broadway. & Julia is a modern and humorous reinterpretation of Shakespeare's classic work Romeo & Juliet, but where the story takes completely new turns and everything is turned on its head. Premiere at Cirkus in Stockholm on February 19, 2026.

The museum’s largest ever exhibition initiative presents 4,000 artefacts and images in an epic and visual presentation of Nordic cultural history built on the real objects and stories collected by the museum during 150 years.

Flatenbastun offers a relaxed lakeside sauna experience by Lake Flaten in southern Stockholm. Here, warmth, nature and refreshing swims come together in a social and welcoming setting for both regulars and first-time guests. Open sauna sessions are available year-round and booked in advance via the website. Bring swimwear and towels for a genuine Swedish sauna experience close to nature.

The internationally acclaimed drag icon Sasha Velour (RuPaul’s Drag Race) returns to Sweden with her new theatrical production Travesty. Travesty traces hidden queer history across a single site through time — a witch burned in a field, a clown building a theatre, an underground gay bar rising up against the police.

Ulf Stureson performs at Debaser Nova on May 13 with an intimate and deeply personal concert. With a stripped-down setup focused on piano and lyrics, the music explores themes of grief, loss and healing. Rooted in the passing of his partner Lina Selleby, the performance creates a reflective space where the audience is invited into a moment of quiet intensity and emotional connection.

Hornstulls Marknad is a public market taking place every Saturday and Sunday, from the first weekend of April to the last weekend in September (except for the midsummer weekend in June). Flea, vintage, design, art, crafts, antiques, literature, delicatessen, foodstuffs and much more.

BAUHAUS-Galan is an annual world-class athletics gala held at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. Many of the competitors consider the Stadium to be the world's most beautiful arena. The world elite is always present, competing against Sweden’s best track and field athletes. The atmosphere at the Stadium is always magical, with its history combined with modern technology and an audience seated just one meter from the competitors.

The adidas Stockholm Marathon takes you through the streets of a beautiful European capital built on 14 islands. The course of this race offers spectacular views of a unique city with varied scenery, including nature and an impeccably preserved medieval city center. The enthusiastic crowds will cheer you along the route and lead you to an unforgettable finish at the 1912 Olympic Stadium, the home of 83 officially recognized world records in athletics. No other arena in the world comes close to that number and hopefully, you can have your own record finishing the adidas Stockholm Marathon at this stadium.

With our very popular 'Do it Yourself' sessions, you can throw as much (or as little) as you want, create at a speed that works for you, practice specific techniques or just throw for the sake of throwing - All on your own time and under your terms! Instructions are not included. If you would like instructions for how to create ceramics please book a workshop or a course. We do not teach during the Do It yourself sessions.

An exhibition by contemporary artist Alia Ali, who works across photography, video, and installation. Known for her visually striking photographic works in which body, textile, and identity intertwine, Ali explores in the exhibition Scapes the boundaries between the individual and the collective, and between visibility and anonymity. Her work has previously been exhibited internationally in the United States, Africa, and the Middle East, an this exhibition marks her debut in Sweden.

Äventyrs is the world's first museum that depicts adventures from all over the world - created to inspire our visitors, awaken dreams and ignite the spark for adventure. In addition to several inspiring exhibitions, there is a large adventure shop and a cafe. Äventyrs also offer an adventure community, education and lectures. The museum is temporary ("pop-up") until midsummer, but hopefully it can remain for longer!

Welcome to Stockholm’s folkmusic oasis: Skeppis – the house of folk music! The unique cultural space hosts jam sessions, concerts, workshops, social dancing to live acoustic music, food, and drinks (non-alcoholic). Open to all newcomers, beginners and experienced visitors. The venue offers a variety of activities, and everything is run non-profit in the spirit of folkmusic!

Expect street food, workshops, talks, and activities for all ages.
